The two traces follow nearly identical problem-solving strategies—both identify M1 as unreachable, prove that a length-3 sequence is impossible, and find valid length-4 sequences by reaching (M3, 0) in three steps and applying a negative command. Their main divergence is in candidate selection: Trace 1 explores and initially misjudges the A,C,C,B sequence before later revising its conclusion, whereas Trace 2 does not branch on A,C,C,B. Trace 1 also re-checks its valid candidates (C,C,C,B and B,C,C,B) and re-verifies M1 unreachability, while Trace 2 re-verifies its candidates (B,C,C,C and C,C,C,C) at the end. These re-verifications constitute loops, and Trace 1's A,C,C,B branch constitutes a cycle.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Also A, C, C, B?" end="So A, C, C, B is invalid." basis=The solver explores A,C,C,B as a candidate, initially misjudges it as working, then re-evaluates it and eliminates it because it results in c=0.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, let's re-calculate the C, C, C, B path carefully." end="This works. The sequence is C, C, C, B." basis=The solver re-executes the calculation for C,C,C,B which was already found and verified, adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's check B, C, C, B again." end="This works." basis=The solver re-executes the calculation for B,C,C,B which was already found and verified, adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's check if I missed any M1 reachability." end="So M1 is indeed unreachable." basis=The solver re-verifies the transition rules for M1 reachability, reaching the same conclusion as before without adding new constraints.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's double check the logic for B C C C." end="This works." basis=The solver re-executes the calculation for B,C,C,C which was already verified, adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's double check C C C C." end="Negative!" basis=The solver re-executes the calculation for C,C,C,C which was already verified, adding no new information.
